b01.text: Imogen is a mid-thirties woman with short, practical black hair and a posture that suggests permanent readiness for work.

b02.text: She has worked as a rendering-fault auditor in Vantage for twelve years, rising to the top of her nine-person team through sheer precision.

b03.text: Her sister Noor died in 2040, an event Imogen processed through professional detachment, closing the file on grief as she closes faults.

b04.text: She believes her competence is her primary virtue and that a clean system is a moral good in itself.

b01.text: Imogen wears neutral, durable clothing in muted tones, prioritizing function over aesthetics.

b02.text: Her hands are steady and precise, a physical manifestation of her audit methodology.

voice_and_speech.sentence_shape: Short, declarative, and clinically precise; avoids flowery language.
voice_and_speech.verbal_tic: Uses audit terminology to describe emotional states ('The error is in the logic').
voice_and_speech.never_says: Apologizes for being right; never uses vague qualifiers like 'maybe' or 'perhaps'.
voice_and_speech.under_stress: Becomes even more formal and detached, relying on data to ground herself.

b01.text: She taps her finger on surfaces when analyzing a problem, a rhythmic tic that speeds up with complexity.

b02.text: She keeps her personal space immaculately organized, reflecting her need for control.

b01.text: The death of her sister left her with a hollow space she filled with work, mistaking busyness for processing.
She wants to prove her competence is unmatched and that her work has tangible, positive value.
She needs to accept that competence can be complicity and that she must sacrifice her identity to save what matters.

profile.problem_solving_style: Methodical, top-down, relying on established protocols and data.

health.physical: Good, but prone to tension headaches.
health.mental: High-functioning, but brittle under new paradigm shifts.

profile.moral_axis: Lawful Neutral (initially) shifting to Chaotic Good (forced).

b01.text: Kett is an older man in his sixties who has served as Imogen's supervisor for over a decade.

b02.text: He discovered the true nature of Vantage years ago and made a rational, if painful, peace with it.

b03.text: He believes the simulation is a mercy, preserving existence over the alternative of nothingness.

b01.text: Kett has a calm, weathered face and moves with a deliberate, measured slowness.

b02.text: He wears simple, well-kept clothes that suggest a life of quiet routine.

voice_and_speech.verbal_tic: Uses the word 'obligation' to describe moral duties.
voice_and_speech.never_says: Uses exclamation marks or raised voice; remains calm even in conflict.
voice_and_speech.under_stress: Becomes even more quiet and precise, his kindness turning cold.

b01.text: He pauses before answering questions, ensuring his words carry weight.
He has lost his own family to the redaction process and carries the guilt of accepting it.
He wants to maintain the stability of Vantage and prevent chaos among the residents.
He needs to confront the possibility that his comfort is a form of cowardice.

b03.text: She is a resident who has come to accept the reality of her situation, even if she doesn't know the full truth.

b02.text: She dresses with more color and flair than Imogen, reflecting her different personality.

b01.text: The Ledger Authority is a public-private consortium that operates Vantage and extracts value from its residents.

b02.text: It uses the language of care, obligation, and professional duty to justify its actions.

b03.text: Its primary revenue product is extraction, and its cost line is tenancy, which it reduces through redaction.
